explanation: The fleet action decided what the siege could be. The Chesapeake article, at revision 1370598769: “The strategically decisive battle prevented the Royal Navy from reinforcing or evacuating the besieged British army of Lieutenant-general Lord Cornwallis at Yorktown, Virginia. With its victory, the French navy was able to gain control over local sea lanes and provided the Franco-American besiegers with siege artillery and troops reinforcements. These proved decisive in securing Cornwallis’ surrender.” The Yorktown article states it from the other end at revision 1376522207: “As a result of this victory, de Grasse blocked any reinforcement or escape by sea for Cornwallis and also disembarked the heavy siege guns required by the allied land forces.” `enabled` and not `caused`: the siege was already being marched to — Washington and Rochambeau arrived on 28 September — and what the battle decided was that it could be pressed and not relieved. `probable`, on the two articles alone (rule 22).
